title: Why False Stories Travel Faster
subtitle: 假消息為什麼跑得比真相快
source: 原創教學文章；研究數據依 Vosoughi, Roy & Aral (2018), Science 及 MIT News 報導，2026-10-21 核對

sources.title: Vosoughi, Roy & Aral (2018). The spread of true and false news online. Science, 359(6380).
MIT News (2018-03-08). Study: On Twitter, false news travels faster than true stories.

beginner.title: The Message That Ran Faster
paras: Imagine two messages arrive on your phone at the same time. One is true but a little boring. The other is surprising and exciting — and false. Which one will your friends share first? Many people guess the true one. A large study suggests the answer is the false one.
想像兩則訊息同時傳到你的手機。一則是真的，但有點無聊；另一則令人驚訝又刺激——但是假的。你的朋友會先轉傳哪一則？很多人猜是真的那則。但一項大型研究指出，答案是假的那則。

In 2018, three researchers at MIT published a study in the journal Science. They looked at about 126,000 news stories that spread on Twitter between 2006 and 2017. About three million people shared these stories more than 4.5 million times. Six fact-checking groups had already decided whether each story was true or false, so the researchers had reliable evidence about every story.
2018 年，三位麻省理工學院（MIT）的研究者在《科學》期刊發表了一項研究。他們分析了 2006 到 2017 年間在 Twitter 上流傳的約 12 萬 6 千則新聞，約三百萬人把這些新聞轉發了超過 450 萬次。六個事實查核組織早已判定每則新聞是真是假，所以研究者對每則新聞都有可靠的證據。

The results were clear. False stories were 70 percent more likely to be shared again than true ones. True stories took about six times longer to reach 1,500 people. In other words, a rumor could travel across the network while the truth was still getting ready.
結果很清楚。假新聞被再次轉發的機率比真新聞高 70%；真新聞觸及 1,500 人所花的時間，大約是假新聞的六倍。換句話說，謠言已經傳遍整個網路，真相還在準備出門。

Why does this happen? The researchers found that false news often felt new and surprising. People enjoy sharing something new, because it makes them look like they know something first. Many replies to false stories showed surprise and disgust. Robots, or “bots”, were not the main problem. When the researchers removed them, the result stayed the same. People spread most of the false news.
為什麼會這樣？研究者發現，假新聞常常讓人覺得新鮮又意外。人們喜歡分享新東西，因為這讓自己看起來比別人先知道。許多對假新聞的回應都帶著驚訝和厭惡。機器人帳號（bots）並不是主要問題：研究者把它們移除後，結果還是一樣。散播大部分假新聞的，是人。

This means that each of us is part of the answer. Before you share a story, you can stop and ask a few questions. Who wrote it? Is the writer anonymous? Is there evidence, or only strong feelings? Does the headline exaggerate? A few seconds of checking can slow down a false story.
這代表我們每個人都是解答的一部分。轉傳一則消息前，你可以停下來問幾個問題：誰寫的？作者是匿名的嗎？有證據，還是只有強烈的情緒？標題有沒有誇大？幾秒鐘的查證，就能讓一則假消息跑慢一點。

intermediate.title: Why False Stories Travel Faster
paras: Picture two posts appearing in your feed at the same moment. One reports an ordinary but accurate fact; the other makes a shocking claim that turns out to be false. If you had to bet on which one would be shared more widely, which would you choose? Most of us would like to believe that truth has the advantage. A landmark study, however, suggests the opposite.
想像兩則貼文同時出現在你的動態上。一則報導一個平凡但正確的事實；另一則提出驚人的說法，後來證明是假的。如果要你賭哪一則會被分享得更廣，你會選哪一則？我們大多希望相信真相占上風。然而，一項里程碑式的研究顯示，事實正好相反。

In 2018, MIT researchers Soroush Vosoughi, Deb Roy and Sinan Aral published one of the largest studies of how news spreads online. They tracked roughly 126,000 stories that circulated on Twitter between 2006 and 2017, shared more than 4.5 million times by about three million people. To decide which stories were true, they relied on six independent fact-checking organizations, whose judgments agreed more than 95 percent of the time.
2018 年，MIT 研究者 Soroush Vosoughi、Deb Roy 和 Sinan Aral 發表了一項關於新聞如何在網路上傳播的大型研究。他們追蹤了 2006 到 2017 年間在 Twitter 上流傳的約 12 萬 6 千則新聞，這些新聞被約三百萬人轉發超過 450 萬次。為了判斷哪些是真的，他們採用六個獨立事實查核組織的判定，這些組織的判斷有超過 95% 的時候是一致的。

The gap between true and false news was striking. False stories were 70 percent more likely to be retweeted than true ones, and true stories needed about six times as long to reach 1,500 people. Political news spread especially fast. As one of the researchers put it, falsehood diffuses “significantly farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth.”
真假新聞之間的差距非常驚人。假新聞被轉推的機率比真新聞高 70%，而真新聞要花大約六倍的時間才能觸及 1,500 人。政治新聞傳得特別快。正如其中一位研究者所說，假消息的擴散「比真相傳得更遠、更快、更深、也更廣，而且差距顯著」。

What gives false news this speed? The researchers point to novelty. False stories tended to be more surprising, and people who share surprising information can appear to be “in the know.” Replies to false stories expressed more surprise and disgust, while replies to true stories showed more sadness, anticipation and trust. Notably, automated accounts were not to blame: when bots were removed from the data, the difference remained. The study does not prove that novelty alone causes sharing, but it suggests that human choices, rather than machines, drive the problem.
是什麼讓假新聞跑得這麼快？研究者指向「新奇感」。假新聞往往更令人意外，而分享意外消息的人，看起來就像是「消息靈通」的人。對假新聞的回應表達了較多的驚訝與厭惡，對真新聞的回應則較多悲傷、期待與信任。值得注意的是，自動化帳號並不是元兇：把機器人帳號從資料中移除後，差距依然存在。這項研究並沒有證明新奇感本身就會導致分享，但它顯示推動問題的是人的選擇，而不是機器。

If people are the main reason false news spreads, people can also be part of the solution. Before sharing, it is worth asking where a story comes from, whether its source is anonymous, and whether it offers evidence or simply an emotional reaction. Headlines that exaggerate or sound too perfect deserve a second look. Slowing down for a moment may feel small, but across millions of users, small pauses add up.
如果人是假新聞擴散的主因，人也可以是解方的一部分。分享之前，值得問一問：這則消息從哪裡來？來源是不是匿名的？它提供了證據，還是只有情緒反應？誇大其詞或聽起來太完美的標題，值得多看一眼。停下來一下或許微不足道，但在數百萬使用者之間，這些小小的停頓會累積起來。

advanced.title: The Speed of a Story
paras: We like to imagine that information markets reward accuracy — that, given enough time and enough readers, true claims will outcompete false ones. Yet the architecture of social media complicates this comforting assumption. When any user can broadcast to an audience of thousands, the question is no longer simply what is true, but what is likely to be passed on.
我們喜歡想像資訊市場會獎勵正確——只要時間夠長、讀者夠多，真的說法終究會勝過假的。然而，社群媒體的結構讓這個令人安心的假設變得複雜。當任何使用者都能向成千上萬的觀眾廣播，問題就不再只是「什麼是真的」，而是「什麼可能被傳下去」。

A 2018 study in Science by Soroush Vosoughi, Deb Roy and Sinan Aral offered one of the most detailed answers to that question. Drawing on Twitter’s archive, the authors examined roughly 126,000 news cascades — unbroken chains of retweets — that were shared more than 4.5 million times by about three million people between 2006 and 2017. Crucially, they did not judge the stories themselves; they relied on six independent fact-checking organizations whose verdicts overlapped more than 95 percent of the time. Politics was the largest category, with about 45,000 cascades, followed by urban legends, business, terrorism, science, entertainment and natural disasters.

Soroush Vosoughi、Deb Roy 與 Sinan Aral 在 2018 年發表於《科學》的研究，為這個問題提供了最詳盡的答案之一。作者利用 Twitter 的歷史資料，分析了約 12 萬 6 千個新聞「轉推鏈」（不間斷的轉推串），這些內容在 2006 到 2017 年間被約三百萬人轉發超過 450 萬次。關鍵在於，他們沒有自己判斷新聞真假，而是採用六個獨立事實查核組織的判定，這些判定有超過 95% 的時候相互一致。政治是最大的類別，約有 4 萬 5 千個轉推鏈，其次是都市傳說、商業、恐怖主義、科學、娛樂和天然災害。

Their central finding was unambiguous: falsehood diffuses “significantly farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth” across every category of information. False stories were 70 percent more likely to be retweeted, and accurate stories took roughly six times as long to reach 1,500 people. Measured by depth, falsehoods reached ten steps along a retweet chain about twenty times faster than facts did. The effect was strongest for political news, an area in which a claim can mislead the public long before any correction appears.
他們的核心發現毫不含糊：在每一類資訊中，假消息的擴散都「比真相傳得更遠、更快、更深、也更廣，而且差距顯著」。假新聞被轉推的機率高出 70%，正確的新聞則要花大約六倍時間才能觸及 1,500 人。若以深度衡量，假消息沿著轉推鏈傳到第十層的速度，大約是事實的二十倍。這個效應在政治新聞上最強烈——在這個領域裡，一個說法可能在任何更正出現之前，早已誤導了大眾。

The more unsettling result concerned responsibility. Automated bots spread true and false stories at similar rates, so removing them did not change the overall pattern; the difference was driven by human users. The authors proposed a “novelty hypothesis”: false stories were measurably more novel, and the replies they attracted expressed more surprise and disgust, whereas replies to true stories leaned towards sadness, anticipation and trust. Sharing novel information may confer social status, signaling that one is “in the know.” The researchers were careful, however, to state that they could not claim novelty causes retweets — a distinction between correlation and causation that is easily lost when findings are retold.

更令人不安的結果與責任有關。自動化機器人帳號散播真假新聞的速度差不多，所以把它們移除後，整體模式並沒有改變；造成差距的是人類使用者。作者提出「新奇假說」：假新聞在可測量的程度上更新奇，引來的回應也表達了更多驚訝與厭惡；對真新聞的回應則偏向悲傷、期待與信任。分享新奇資訊可能帶來社會地位，暗示自己是「消息靈通」的人。不過研究者很謹慎地說明，他們不能斷言新奇感導致了轉推——這種相關與因果的區別，在研究結果被轉述時很容易消失。

If the problem is behavioral rather than merely technological, then solutions must be partly behavioral too. As Aral observed, if bots alone were to blame, a technological fix might be enough; because people are the main drivers, behavioral interventions become even more important. Fact-checking labels, slower sharing features and media-literacy education all aim to insert a moment of reflection between seeing and sharing. None of these is a complete remedy, and a study limited to one platform cannot settle how far its patterns generalize. Its lasting contribution may be to reveal an uncomfortable truth: the speed of a story tells us little about whether it is true, and a great deal about ourselves.

如果問題出在行為，而不只是技術，那麼解方也必須有一部分來自行為。正如 Aral 所說，如果只是機器人帳號的問題，技術就能解決；正因為主要推手是人，行為上的介入就更加重要。事實查核標籤、放慢分享的功能、媒體素養教育，目的都是在「看到」與「分享」之間插入片刻的思考。這些都不是萬靈丹，而一項只研究單一平台的研究，也無法斷定它的發現能推廣到多遠。它最持久的貢獻，或許是揭露了一個令人不安的事實：一則故事傳得多快，幾乎說明不了它是否為真，卻說明了很多關於我們自己的事。

vocab.example: Is there any evidence for this claim?
The rumor spread across the school in an hour.
The post came from an anonymous account.
The novelty of the idea attracted attention.
A falsehood can spread faster than a correction.
Anyone can broadcast an opinion online.
The video reached a huge audience.
A chart can mislead readers without a single lie.
The data reveal a clear pattern.

phrases.usage: 用來換個方式說明前一句，通常更簡單或更直接。
phrases.example: The test was optional. In other words, nobody had to take it.
phrases.writing: S + V. In other words, S + V.

phrases.usage: turn out to be + N／adj.：事後才發現的結果。
phrases.example: The shocking news turned out to be false.
phrases.writing: What seemed ... turned out to be ...

phrases.meaning: 消息靈通的、知道內幕的
phrases.usage: be in the know；偏口語，帶「圈內人」的意味。
phrases.example: She always seems to be in the know about school events.
phrases.writing: People who ... appear to be in the know.

phrases.usage: small things add up：小事累積起來會有大影響。另有「說得通」的意思（It doesn’t add up.）。
phrases.example: Ten minutes a day adds up over a year.
phrases.writing: Small ... may seem minor, but they add up.

phrases.meaning: 值得再看一眼、值得再檢查
phrases.usage: deserve + N：值得……；a second look 指再次仔細檢查。
phrases.example: Any headline that sounds too perfect deserves a second look.
phrases.writing: Claims that ... deserve a second look.

patterns.frame: A is + 數字 + percent more likely to + V than B
patterns.meaning: A 比 B 更可能……（多出幾成）
patterns.example: False stories were 70 percent more likely to be shared than true ones.
patterns.tip: more likely 後面接 to + 原形動詞；than 後面比較的對象要對等（stories 對 ones）。

patterns.frame: A take(s) + 倍數 + as long to + V
patterns.example: True stories took about six times as long to reach 1,500 people.
patterns.tip: six times as long（六倍長）和 six times longer 在口語常混用，但正式寫作建議用 as long。

patterns.example: Before sharing, it is worth asking where a story comes from.
patterns.tip: worth 後面接 V-ing 或名詞，不接 to + V（✗ It is worth to ask）。

patterns.frame: S + do(es) not prove that ..., but it suggests that ...
patterns.example: The study does not prove that novelty causes sharing, but it suggests that human choices matter.
patterns.tip: 區分「證明」和「顯示」：研究推論不要寫成定論。

quote.text: Falsehood flies, and truth comes limping after it.
quote.author: Jonathan Swift
quote.work: The Examiner, 9 November 1710（Story Quest Week 1 Day 3 也引用這一句）

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to write news stories for Twitter.
A study showing that false stories spread faster than true ones.
Why robots share most of the false news.
How MIT checks every story on the internet.
beginner.evidence: False stories were 70 percent more likely to be shared again than true ones.
beginner.why: 全文：大型研究發現假新聞傳得比真新聞快，主因是人。
traps: 捏造：文中沒談怎麼寫新聞。
正反顛倒：原文 Robots … were not the main problem。
張冠李戴：判斷真假的是六個事實查核機構。

beginner.q: What does “them” in “When the researchers removed them” in the fourth paragraph refer to?
options: Replies showing disgust.
False stories.
The researchers.
Robots, or “bots”.
beginner.evidence: Robots, or “bots”, were not the main problem.
beginner.why: 前一句提到機器人帳號，被移除的就是它們。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：回應只是觀察到的現象。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：假新聞是被研究的對象。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：研究者是做移除的人。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: True stories took about six times longer to reach 1,500 people.
False stories were six times more likely to be shared again.
The study looked at about 1,500 news stories.
The researchers decided themselves which stories were true.
beginner.evidence: True stories took about six times longer to reach 1,500 people.
traps: 數字錯位：被轉傳的機率高 70%，「六倍」是到達 1,500 人的時間。
數字錯位：研究看了約 126,000 則。
張冠李戴：是六個事實查核機構判定的。

beginner.q: What does the writer suggest each of us can do?
options: Remove all robots from social media.
Share surprising stories as quickly as possible.
Check a story for a few seconds before sharing it.
Stop reading the news on our phones.
beginner.evidence: A few seconds of checking can slow down a false story.
beginner.why: 最後一段：分享前花幾秒查證。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：移除機器人後結果不變。
正反顛倒：這正是假新聞傳得快的原因。
過度推論：作者沒叫人不看新聞。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Automated accounts are the main source of false stories.
Political news is the only kind of news that spreads online.
False news spreads faster than true news, mainly because of human choices.
Fact-checking organizations rarely agree with each other.
intermediate.evidence: it suggests that human choices, rather than machines, drive the problem
intermediate.why: 第三、四段：假新聞傳得快，驅動者是人而不是機器。
traps: 正反顛倒：移除機器人後差異仍在。
以偏概全：政治新聞只是傳得特別快的一類。
正反顛倒：它們的判斷一致率超過 95%。

intermediate.q: What does the phrase “in the know” in the fourth paragraph mean?
options: Having information that others do not have yet.
Being unable to tell true from false.
Working for a fact-checking group.
Feeling sad after reading the news.
intermediate.evidence: people who share surprising information can appear to be “in the know.”
intermediate.why: 分享新奇資訊的人看起來「消息靈通」。
traps: 正反顛倒：重點是看起來知道得多。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：查核機構是判斷真假的單位。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：悲傷是對「真新聞」的回應。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The study tracked stories on Twitter for only one year.
Replies to false stories showed more trust and sadness.
The six fact-checkers agreed less than half of the time.
Replies to true stories showed more sadness, anticipation and trust.
intermediate.evidence: replies to true stories showed more sadness, anticipation and trust
traps: 張冠李戴：假新聞的回應是驚訝和厭惡。
數字錯位：一致率超過 95%。

intermediate.q: What can be inferred from the fourth paragraph?
options: Removing bots made false news disappear almost completely.
The study does not show for certain that novelty causes sharing.
Surprising stories that people share are always false.
People share news mainly to make their friends feel sad.
intermediate.evidence: The study does not prove that novelty alone causes sharing
intermediate.why: 第四段最後：研究並未證明新奇性單獨造成分享。
traps: 正反顛倒：移除後差異仍在。
以偏概全：只是假新聞「往往」比較新奇。
捏造：文中說分享新奇事讓人看起來消息靈通。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To compare Twitter with other social media platforms.
To explain how to build a reliable fact-checking website.
To prove that social media should be banned for students.
To report how false news spreads and what this says about human behavior.
advanced.evidence: the speed of a story tells us little about whether it is true, and a great deal about ourselves
advanced.why: 全文介紹研究結果，最後指出傳播速度反映的是人的行為。
traps: 正反顛倒：作者說只研究一個平台，無法斷定能否推論。
捏造：文中沒談架網站。
捏造：作者沒有這樣主張。

advanced.q: What does “cascades” refer to in the second paragraph?
options: Waterfalls in the natural world.
Unbroken chains of retweets.
Groups of fact-checkers.
Categories of news topics.
advanced.evidence: roughly 126,000 news cascades — unbroken chains of retweets
advanced.why: 破折號後面直接解釋：連續不斷的轉推鏈。
traps: 字面誤讀：cascade 原意是瀑布，這裡是比喻。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：查核機構是判斷真假的單位。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：類別是用來分類 cascades 的。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Science was the largest category of cascades.
Bots spread false stories much faster than true ones.
Bots spread true and false stories at similar rates.
The researchers proved that novelty causes retweets.
advanced.evidence: Automated bots spread true and false stories at similar rates
traps: 張冠李戴：最大類別是政治。
正反顛倒：機器人傳真假的速度差不多。
正反顛倒：原文 they could not claim novelty causes retweets。

advanced.q: According to Aral, why are behavioral interventions especially important?
options: Because people, not bots, are the main drivers of false news.
Because technology cannot detect any of the false stories.
Because fact-checking labels have already failed on Twitter.
Because political news no longer spreads very quickly.
advanced.evidence: because people are the main drivers, behavioral interventions become even more important
traps: 捏造：文中沒有這種說法。
正反顛倒：作者說它們不是完整解方，不是失敗。
正反顛倒：政治新聞的效應最強。

reflections: Think of a time you almost shared something that turned out to be false. What made it feel believable?
Design one rule for your class group chat that could slow down rumors without stopping real news.

videos.title: How false news can spread
videos.desc: An animated lesson on circular reporting: how one unchecked claim can be repeated by source after source until it looks true.
videos.zh: 動畫課程：「循環報導」如何讓一個未查證的說法被層層轉述，最後看起來像真的。
videos.question: Have you ever seen a claim that seemed true only because many sources repeated it?

videos.title: How we can protect truth in the age of misinformation
videos.desc: One of the authors of the Science study discusses false news and what we can do about it.
videos.zh: 這篇文章所引研究的作者之一，談假消息與我們能做些什麼。
videos.question: Which of the speaker’s ideas could work in a school setting?

videos.title: Why people fall for misinformation
videos.desc: An animated lesson on why our minds can be fooled by false information.
videos.zh: 動畫課程：為什麼我們的大腦會被錯誤資訊騙過。
videos.question: What habit of mind makes you more likely to believe a false story?

paras: We like to imagine that, given enough time, true claims will win out over false ones. Yet social media complicates this comforting belief. When any user can share a post with thousands of people, the question is no longer simply what is true, but what is likely to be passed on.
我們喜歡想像：只要時間夠久，真話終究會勝過假話。然而社群媒體讓這個令人安心的想法變得複雜。當任何使用者都能把貼文分享給成千上萬人，問題就不再只是什麼是真的，而是什麼比較可能被傳下去。

A 2018 study in the journal Science by Soroush Vosoughi, Deb Roy and Sinan Aral offered one of the most detailed answers. Drawing on Twitter’s archive, the researchers examined about 126,000 news “cascades” (unbroken chains of retweets) that were shared more than 4.5 million times by about three million people between 2006 and 2017. Crucially, they did not judge the stories themselves — they relied on six independent fact-checking organizations, whose verdicts agreed more than 95 percent of the time.
2018 年，沃索吉、羅伊和阿拉爾在《科學》期刊發表的研究，提供了最詳細的答案之一。研究者利用推特的資料庫，分析了約 12 萬 6 千個新聞「轉推鏈」（連續不斷的轉推串），它們在 2006 到 2017 年間被大約三百萬人分享了超過 450 萬次。關鍵在於，他們不自己判斷新聞真假，而是依靠六個獨立的事實查核機構，而這些機構的判斷有超過 95% 的時候一致。

Their central finding was clear: false news spread farther, faster, deeper and more broadly than the truth in every category. False stories were 70 percent more likely to be retweeted, and true stories took about six times as long to reach 1,500 people. The effect was strongest for political news, an area in which a false claim can mislead the public long before any correction appears.
他們的核心發現很明確：在每一類新聞中，假新聞都比真相傳得更遠、更快、更深、更廣。假新聞被轉推的機率高出 70%，真新聞要花大約六倍的時間才能傳到 1,500 人。這個效應在政治新聞上最強——在這個領域，假消息可能在任何更正出現之前，就已經誤導了大眾。

More unsettling was the question of responsibility. Automated accounts, or bots, spread true and false stories at similar rates, so removing them did not change the overall pattern; the difference was driven by human users. The authors pointed to novelty: false stories were more surprising, and the replies they attracted expressed more surprise and disgust, whereas replies to true stories leaned towards sadness, anticipation and trust. Sharing something new may make a person look “in the know.” The researchers were careful, however, to say that they could not prove novelty causes sharing.
更令人不安的是責任歸屬的問題。自動帳號，也就是機器人，傳播真假新聞的速度差不多，所以把它們移除並沒有改變整體模式；造成差異的是人類使用者。作者指出新奇性的作用：假新聞比較令人驚訝，引來的回應表現出更多驚訝與厭惡，而真新聞的回應則偏向悲傷、期待和信任。分享新東西可能讓人看起來「消息靈通」。不過研究者很謹慎，說他們無法證明新奇性會造成分享。

If the problem lies with people rather than machines, then the solutions must involve people too. As Aral observed, a technical fix might be enough if bots alone were to blame; because humans are the main drivers, changing behaviour becomes even more important. So simple are some of the proposed tools, such as fact-checking labels and features that slow down sharing, that they aim only to add a moment of reflection between seeing and sharing. None is a complete remedy. Still, the study reveals an uncomfortable truth: the speed of a story tells us little about whether it is true, and a great deal about ourselves.
如果問題出在人而不是機器，解方也必須和人有關。阿拉爾指出，如果只是機器人的錯，技術上的修補或許就夠了；但既然人才是主要推手，改變行為就更加重要。有些提議的工具簡單到只是想在「看到」和「分享」之間加入一刻思考，例如事實查核標籤和讓分享變慢的功能。沒有一種是完整的解方。即便如此，這項研究揭露了一個令人不安的真相：一則消息傳得多快，幾乎無法告訴我們它是不是真的，卻能透露很多關於我們自己的事。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A study showing false news spreads faster, mainly because of people.
How to build a reliable fact-checking organization.
Why bots are the main cause of false news online.
How political news is written for social media.
questions.evidence: the difference was driven by human users
questions.why: 全文：大型研究發現假新聞傳得比真相快，推手是人而不是機器人。
traps: 捏造：查核機構只是研究判斷真假的依據。
正反顛倒：移除機器人後模式不變。
以偏概全：政治新聞只是效應最強的一類。

questions.q: What does “them” in “removing them did not change the overall pattern” refer to?
options: The replies showing surprise and disgust.
The six fact-checking organizations.
Automated accounts, or bots.
The true stories that spread slowly.
questions.evidence: Automated accounts, or bots, spread true and false stories at similar rates
questions.why: 同一句前半：被移除的是機器人帳號。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：回應是後面描述的現象。
時序錯置：查核機構在第二段。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：真新聞是被比較的對象。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: False stories were six times more likely to be retweeted.
True stories took about six times as long to reach 1,500 people.
The researchers judged each story’s truth by themselves.
Bots spread false stories much faster than true ones.
questions.evidence: true stories took about six times as long to reach 1,500 people
traps: 數字錯位：被轉推的機率高 70%，六倍是到達 1,500 人的時間。
正反顛倒：他們依靠六個查核機構。
正反顛倒：機器人傳真假新聞的速度差不多。

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a feeling expressed in replies to true stories?
options: Trust.
Sadness.
Anticipation.
Disgust.
questions.evidence: whereas replies to true stories leaned towards sadness, anticipation and trust
questions.why: 對真新聞的回應是悲傷、期待和信任；厭惡是對假新聞的回應。
traps: 有提到：trust。
有提到：sadness。
有提到：anticipation。

mixed.prompt: False stories were 70 percent more likely to be [47], and the authors suggested that their [48] might help explain why people shared them.
mixed.why: 第一格出自第三段 more likely to be retweeted（被動）；第二格出自第四段 novelty。

mixed.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage? Choose ALL that apply.
options: About 126,000 news cascades were examined.
The fact-checkers agreed more than 95 percent of the time.
The researchers proved that novelty causes sharing.
The effect was strongest for political news.
Removing bots made false news disappear.
The study covered news shared on Facebook.
mixed.why: A、B 第二段；D 第三段。C 正反顛倒（無法證明）；E 正反顛倒（模式沒變）；F 張冠李戴（是推特）。

mixed.q: Which phrase in the second paragraph explains what a news cascade is?
